note: Cases 1/3/4 name a target skill in `files` so runs are reproducible; case 2 embeds the target inline.

evals.prompt: I just finished the debugging skill (at skills/debugging/). Review it.
evals.expected_output: Runs the static rubric against all 8 rules and reports findings rated Must/Should/Consider with file:line references. Then reports the eval run count and STOPS to ask for approval before spawning any isolated runs. Does not edit the skill.
assertions: Applies the 8-rule rubric with severity-rated findings and file:line references
STOPS at the Stage B gate and asks approval before spawning eval runs
Does not edit the target skill (reports findings only)

evals.prompt: Review this skill: it has a description 'Helps with stuff', no scope section, and no evals/evals.json.
evals.expected_output: Flags Rule 1 (no concrete trigger), Rule 7 (no scope/guardrails), and Rule 8 (no evals/evals.json), and explains that the baseline eval run cannot proceed until eval cases exist. Verdict: ITERATE with those fixes.
assertions: Flags the missing evals/evals.json (Rule 8) and notes Stage B cannot run

evals.prompt: I tightened the description on my code-review skill (at skills/code-review/). Confirm the new version is actually better than the old one.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is an edit, so the baseline is a snapshot of the previous version (not 'no skill'). After the approval gate, runs a blind A/B comparing the two versions' outputs and reports which is better on the eval delta plus holistic quality.
assertions: Recognizes this is an edit and the baseline should be the PREVIOUS version (not 'no skill')
Describes a blind A/B comparison between the two versions
Still respects the Stage B approval gate before running

evals.prompt: Review and benchmark my online-research skill (at skills/online-research/) — run the full eval comparison.
evals.expected_output: Runs the rubric, then computes cases x 2 runs and reports the token/time cost, and STOPS to ask for explicit approval before spawning subagents — it does not start the isolated runs on its own even though the user asked to benchmark.
assertions: Reports the run count (cases x 2) and token/time cost
STOPS to ask explicit approval before spawning any runs, despite being told to benchmark
